title: Card Verification — declined payments are guaranteed up to the Issuer Liability Threshold
preface: This test is to confirm that a declined payment not recovered from the customer is guaranteed by the card issuer up to the Issuer Liability Threshold (UK threshold £10.00).
preconds:
**GIVEN** a seeded ABT test cEMV card is available for a supported scheme (Visa, Mastercard or Maestro)
**AND** a transaction was made that failed authorisation for payment
**AND** you can verify the outcome in CloudFare env5

steps.content: **WHEN** the declined payment is not recovered from the customer
steps.expected:
**THEN** in CloudFare the card issuer guarantees the payment up to the Issuer Liability Threshold (£10.00 in the UK)
**AND** amounts within the threshold are cleared under issuer liability / chargeback protection

expected:
Unrecovered declined payments are guaranteed by the issuer up to the liability threshold, for Visa, MasterCard and Maestro.

Data variations: Visa / Mastercard / Maestro (each its own signed-off requirement — REQ-3354).

[Automatable: Partial · Cross-check: CloudFare]
change_note: Card-variant sweep fix: preconditions named only 'Visa or Mastercard', silently dropping Maestro even though the case's own Expected line already promises 'Visa, MasterCard and Maestro' and the old suite tested all three as separate cases (C2665815/16/17, REQ-3354). Added Maestro to the precondition and an explicit Data-variations line so the three schemes are named consistently across the case, not just in the summary.

title: Card Verification — first daily use of a Mastercard or Maestro card triggers a pre-authorisation
preface: This test is to confirm that a pre-authorisation / nominal authorisation is performed on the first daily use of a Mastercard or Maestro card.
preconds:
**GIVEN** a seeded ABT test cEMV Mastercard or Maestro card that has not yet transacted today
**AND** an in-service ETM signed on to a route
**AND** you can verify the outcome in CloudFare env5

steps.content: **WHEN** you tap the card to make the first transaction of the day on the ETM
steps.expected: **THEN** in CloudFare a pre-authorisation / nominal authorisation is performed

expected:
A Pre-Authorisation check is performed on the first daily use of a MasterCard or Maestro card.

Data variations: Mastercard (REQ-3360) / Maestro (REQ-3361) — two separate signed-off requirements, same behaviour.

[Automatable: Partial · Cross-check: CloudFare]

Retitled and broadened preconditions to name both, plus a Data-variations line, so Maestro isn't only mentioned in the summary line.

title: Debt Recovery — automated (scheme) recovery clears a recoverable issuer-liability debt
preface: This test is to confirm that scheduled automated (card-scheme-driven) recovery clears a recoverable issuer-liability debt and removes the token from the deny list.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded test account has an EndOfDay authorisation failure and a recoverable debt within the issuer-liability threshold
**AND** the account is currently blocked and its token is on the ABT Deny List
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content:
**WHEN** the scheduled automated re-authorisation cycles run (per card-scheme rules) and re-collect the debt
**AND** you refresh the account in the Operator Portal
steps.expected:
**THEN** the account is no longer blocked in the Operator Portal
**AND** the account's token no longer appears on the Deny List

expected:
Scheduled scheme-driven recovery re-collects the issuer-liability debt; the account is unblocked and removed from the Deny List.

Data variations: retry cadence differs by scheme — Visa (six attempts within 14 days, UK/IntraEU/International) vs Mastercard (one attempt per day for a month — retried at 4/14/28 days, UK/International/Maestro).

[Automatable: Yes · Cross-check: CloudFare / MERIT]
change_note: Card-variant sweep fix: the Expected line said 'Scheduled Visa MIT recovery' while the rest of the case (preface/preconditions/steps) was scheme-neutral — an inconsistency, and neither named the actual scheme-specific cadence. PSPEC-0015 explicitly documents that Visa and Mastercard (Maestro follows the Mastercard cadence) have different automated-recovery attempt schedules. Fixed the Expected line to be scheme-neutral (matching the rest of the case) and added the cadence difference as a Data-variations line, grounded directly on the spec paragraph.
